script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JULIA SITTING AT A TABLE, staring at her laptop. She's in her mid-30s, wearing glasses, and has a determined look on her face. Her phone buzzes. She picks it up.

JULIA
(into phone)
Yes, I understand. I'll be there soon.

She closes her laptop and gathers her things.

INT. APARTMENT BUILDING - LOBBY - DAY

Julia enters the lobby. She's greeted by a middle-aged doorman, MR. GARCIA.

MR. GARCIA
Good morning, Miss Julia. How was your writing session?

JULIA
(smiling)
Good, Mr. Garcia. I'm getting closer.

MR. GARCIA
(encouragingly)
I have no doubt about that. Keep at it.

INT. JULIA'S APARTMENT - DAY

Julia enters her apartment and sets up her laptop on the kitchen table. She begins typing.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Julia is still typing when there's a knock on the door. She hesitates, then gets up to answer it.

It's her neighbor, MIKE, a handsome, charismatic man in his late 20s.

MIKE
(smiling)
Hey, Julia. I saw your light on. Thought I'd check in and see how you were doing.

JULIA
(surprised)
Oh, hi, Mike. I'm fine. Just...working.

MIKE
(looking at her laptop)
Ah, the great American novel. I wish I had your ambition.

JULIA
(smiling)
It's not just about ambition, Mike. It's about persistence and hard work.

MIKE
(leaning against the counter)
Well, I have to admit, I'm impressed. You've been at it for hours.

JULIA
(sighs)
It feels like it. But I won't give up. I have to finish this novel. It's my dream.

MIKE
(nods)
Well, I believe in you. And I'll be here to support you every step of the way.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Julia is sitting at the same table, now with a completed manuscript in front of her. Mr. Garcia walks in and greets her.

MR. GARCIA
(smiling)
Looks like you've finally done it, Miss Julia.

JULIA
(grinning)
I have, Mr. Garcia. I have.

INT. APARTMENT BUILDING - LOBBY - NIGHT

Julia enters the lobby, clutching her manuscript. Mr. Garcia looks up as she approaches.

MR. GARCIA
(excitedly)
Well, well, well. What have we here?

JULIA
(proudly)
I finished it, Mr. Garcia. My novel.

MR. GARCIA
(impressed)
I knew you could do it, Miss Julia. I'm so proud of you.

JULIA
(smiling)
Thank you, Mr. Garcia. But I'm not done yet. I have to find a publisher.

MR. GARCIA
(nods)
I have no doubt you'll do that, too. You have the determination and the talent.

INT. PUBLISHER'S OFFICE - DAY

Julia sits nervously in a waiting room, her manuscript in a neat pile on her lap. A beautiful, stern-faced receptionist, MS. HENDERSON, calls her name.

MS. HENDERSON
(coldly)
Follow me, Miss Julia.

Julia stands up and follows Ms. Henderson into a large office. Sitting behind a desk is a distinguished, older man, PUBLISHER KING.

PUBLISHER KING
(looking up)
Miss Julia. Welcome to our humble abode.

JULIA
(nervously)
Thank you, Mr. King. I've brought my manuscript for your consideration.

PUBLISHER KING
(nods)
Ah, the great American novel. I see you've been working on it for quite some time.

JULIA
(nods)
Yes, I have. I believe it's something special.

PUBLISHER KING
(leaning back in his chair)
Well, Miss Julia, we'll see about that. We receive hundreds of manuscripts a week. Yours will be read and considered, but it's a competitive process.

JULIA
(determinedly)
I understand, Mr. King. But I won't give up. I believe in my novel, and I believe it has the potential to resonate with readers.

PUBLISHER KING
(impressed)
I admire your tenacity, Miss Julia. We'll be in touch.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Julia sits at her usual table, sipping coffee and reading the newspaper. Mr. Garcia enters and joins her.

MR. GARCIA
(smiling)
Well, well, well. It looks like the great American novelist has made it to the front page.

JULIA
(surprised)
What?

MR. GARCIA
(showing her the newspaper)
Your novel, Miss Julia, has been picked up by a major publisher. Congratulations!

JULIA
(ecstatic)
Oh, my goodness. I can't believe it!

MR. GARCIA
(laughs)
Believe it, Miss Julia. You've done it.

INT. APARTMENT BUILDING - LOBBY - NIGHT

Julia enters the lobby, clutching a copy of her published novel. Mr. Garcia looks up as she approaches.

MR. GARCIA
(smiling)
Well, well, well. Look who's made it to the bestseller list.

JULIA
(grinning)
Yes, Mr. Garcia. Yes, I have.

MR. GARCIA
(proudly)
I knew you could do it, Miss Julia.

JULIA
(hugging him)
Thank you, Mr. Garcia. For believing in me.

MR. GARCIA
(laughs)
It's my pleasure, Miss Julia. Now go out there and enjoy your success.

JULIA
(determinedly)
I will, Mr. Garcia. I will.

FADE OUT.
